title: Curation Signal Postmortem: Negative Label Drift and URL Entity Splitters
content:
Summary:
Quick postmortem notes from a spike where we saw an uptick in negative labels for URL-like tokens in the product-id slot. This doc is a scratchpad for heuristics, sample examples, and a candidate relabel pipeline. Not final — keeping short, actionable items for next sync.

What I saw (signal):
- Over the last two weeks our sample-based QA shows negative labels increased from ~2.1% -> ~7.8% on product-id/sku fields across the web-scrape dataset.
- Error mode correlated with long noisy query strings, tracking parameters, and cases where IDs are embedded inside path segments (e.g., /p/ABC-123-xyz).
- Annotators inconsistent: some mark the whole URL as 'product-id', others mark only the segment matching alphanumeric-with-dashes, others abstain.

Why this matters:
- Downstream model training treats product-id as a ground truth feature for canonicalization and deduplication. Drift increases false positives in dedupe and harms QA dashboards.
- Unit economics: bad product-id labels increase dedupe compute and cause human review churn.

Representative examples (raw tokens with current coarse label):
1) https://store.example.com/p/ABC-123-xyz?utm_source=x (labelled NEGATIVE by some annotators; others labelled "product-id")
2) example.com/item?id=SKU:00045-RT (annotator A: product-id=00045-RT; annotator B: abstain)
3) sub.shop.com/c/23/collection/sku_99877 (labelled product-id=sku_99877 by some)
4) api.example.com/v1/products/000-111-222 (labelled product-id entirety by some; others say path is not an isolated id)
5) example.com/track/afg123?redirect=/p/DEF-444 (nested ids, multiple candidates)

Immediate observation: annotators are using two implicit rulesets: (A) 'extract anything that looks like an identifier (alnum/dash/underscore) anywhere in URL' vs (B) 'only label isolated path segments that are canonical-looking IDs when not clearly part of a query param or user slug'.

Proposal: Labeling schema tweak + adjudication heuristics
- Add an explicit field-level guidance paragraph: "For URL-like input, only mark product-id when the token is a standalone path segment or query value that clearly corresponds to a product identifier. Do NOT label entire URLs. If multiple candidate IDs appear, mark the canonical-looking id (prefer path segment over query param) or annotate ALL within the candidate_id_span set with priority ordering."
- Define canonical heuristics (in order of precedence):
  1) Path segment matching regex: (?<![a-zA-Z0-9-])[A-Z0-9]{3,}-[0-9]{2,}(?![a-zA-Z0-9-])  // example pattern for structured SKUs (uppercase-dash-digit)
  2) Named param detection: query params like id, sku, product_id, pid => prefer their values if they match typical SKU patterns.
  3) Word-boundary tokens that include 'sku' or 'product' prefixes (sku_12345) => consider after (1)-(2).
  4) Exclude noisy UTM/ga/utm_* and long base64 tokens (>40 chars) as unlikely product ids.

Adjudication quick rules for overlapping labels:
- If two annotators disagree and one marked entire URL, prefer the narrow span (path segment or query value).
- If multiple candidate ids exist, mark both but add priority tag (primary/secondary) in adjudication sheet. For our training we will use primary only.

Sampling strategy for re-annotation:
- Seed 1: 1000 highest-confidence negatives that match 'contains \bsku|id=|pid=\b' patterns (to see if negatives are false).
- Seed 2: 1000 random URLs from last 30 days ingest where product-id feature is non-null in ingestion pipeline.
- Seed 3: 500 contest cases where two or more candidate_ids are present (nested ids).

Quick regex bank (for annotators/devs):
- product-like path: \b(?:p|product|item|sku|prod|goods|g)\/?([A-Za-z0-9\-_]{4,40})\b
- id param: (?:[?&](?:id|sku|product_id|pid)=)([^&]{2,60})
- exclude long base64: \b[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{41,}\b  (mark as NO)

Labeler UI hints to add (low effort):
- Highlight URL tokens by path vs query; show parsed tokenization so annotator can click the specific segment.
- Quick buttons: 'mark primary id', 'mark secondary id', 'abstain - noisy url'.

Edge cases and debates (notes to self):
- What about merchant slugs that are stable identifiers (e.g., /nike/air-max-270)? Our schema should treat human readable slugs as NOT product-id unless they match known SKU pattern or cross-referenced to catalog.
- Language/locale issues: multi-byte characters in product slugs (JP/KO) — need examples and a separate heuristic.
- When to split host subdomain as brand vs id (shop.brand.com vs brand.com/p/123).

Adjudication workflow (practical):
- Round 0: small adjudication by two senior labelers on 200 sample items across seeds. Record conflicts and expand regexes.
- Round 1: re-label 2,500 items with updated guidance; pay annotators a 10% bonus for careful span work.
- Tracking: add a tiny spreadsheet (linked_artifacts JIRA ticket above) with columns: raw_string | original_labeler | adjudicator | final_label | reason_code | notes.

Training / model implications:
- We may want to emit three derived features for model: primary_id_span, secondary_id_span, id_confidence_score. For training tests, blacklist long base64-looking spans.

Quick TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Draft short 1-paragraph guidance and add to labeling UI (Riley) — target: 2025-03-05
- [ ] Run seed 1 sampling and quick adjudication (Samira) — target: 2025-03-07
- [ ] Add path/query highlighting in annotator UI (ENG ticket PR opened) — Diego to follow up
- [ ] Compile 50 international examples for non-ascii slugs (hold until Round 0 results)

Open questions / experiments to run:
- Is path-segment precedence actually better than query param precedence for our catalog? We should run a small A/B: train dedupe on path-priority vs query-priority labels and measure precision@k.
- For nested ids, what fraction of downstream errors come from choosing wrong candidate? If tiny, maybe simpler rule: always choose first path-candidate.

Notes to future self: keep adjudication conservative. If unsure, prefer narrower spans or abstain. We can always synthesize labels later after model shows consistent mispredictions.

References / related tickets: CONFLUENCE-DataCuration-582 (proto rules), JIRA-DC-4112 (label drift alert), GH PR#78 (UI segment highlight prototype).

End of scratchpad.

(If you read this later: copy core heuristics into the canonical guidelines doc before rolling to full cohort.)
